subject.title: [Bug] Webchat avatar endpoint /avatar/{agentId} returns 404 even with valid IDENTITY.md avatar

question: Should `/avatar/{agentId}` keep generic 404 behavior for missing, too-large, and unsafe local avatars, or should OpenClaw add a user-facing diagnostic path that exposes only redacted reasons?
rationale: The remaining improvement affects a local file-serving endpoint, source redaction, browser UI feedback, and the public avatar contract, so automation should not decide the security/UX boundary silently.

options.title: Add redacted diagnostics
options.body: Expose safe failure reasons through metadata or UI copy while keeping direct image GET generic and preserving workspace containment, size, MIME, auth, and source redaction checks.

options.title: Keep generic 404 only
options.body: Treat the current metadata as sufficient, document the 2 MB limit clearly, and close or reject PRs that try to broaden the endpoint response.

options.title: Adopt a replacement PR
options.body: Sponsor a fresh narrow PR on current main only after the conflicting fork branch is closed or rebuilt without unrelated churn.

recommendation.title: Add redacted diagnostics
recommendation.body: Expose safe failure reasons through metadata or UI copy while keeping direct image GET generic and preserving workspace containment, size, MIME, auth, and source redaction checks.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest history signal for both the avatar feature and the later security hardening around local avatar serving.
